transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, what made me come in today is that my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. Some days I... I completely forget to eat lunch. And then other days, I just stand at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets, even though nothing really tastes right to me anymore. It's just been very strange.
Have you lost any weight recently?

I haven't really stepped on a scale lately to know for sure. Like I was just saying, with the way my eating is all turned around—skipping lunch completely some days and then just grazing on sweets the next—it's hard to tell. I might have lost a little bit, or maybe it just balances out. I just know my appetite is completely off.
Do you ever feel like you're eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's not like I'm sitting down and eating a huge meal all at once. It's more like... just picking at things here and there, like the crackers I mentioned. Just a handful of this or that because I don't really have the drive to make a real meal.
Do you feel like you have less interest in food than you used to?
Yes, I think so. Food just doesn't... it doesn't hold any appeal for me right now. Like I said, nothing really tastes right, so I just don't care about it the way I used to.
Do you find that your eating or not eating is related to how you're feeling emotionally?

Yes, I suppose it is. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, low feeling. It's like... like the color has just gone out of the day before I even get dressed. When I feel that down, I just don't care enough to eat.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried about gaining weight when you do eat?
No, I don't really worry about that. Weight hasn't been on my mind at all, honestly. It's just that the food itself doesn't seem worth the effort.
Do you think your lack of interest in food is related to anything besides your low mood?
No, I don't think so. I mean, it's just the sadness, really. Like I said, things just don't taste right, and I don't have the energy for it. I haven't noticed anything else causing it.
Do you think your eating issues started after your low mood began?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It's a little hard to remember exactly which came first. They just sort of... go together now. I haven't really kept track of the exact timing of it all, so I couldn't say for certain.
Do you feel sad or empty most of the day?
Yes, I do. Most mornings, I wake up with this heavy, low feeling. It's... well, it's just like the color has already gone out of the day before I even get dressed.
How long have you been feeling this low mood?
I'd say this low, colorless feeling has been with me for about a year and two months now. It's just been a steady stretch for that long.
Has your changed eating pattern caused any problems in your daily activities or relationships?

Well, yes, it has. I used to teach craft classes, but I've stopped doing that entirely. And I find myself missing phone calls, appointments, and little family tasks that I used to handle without a second thought. I'm still managing to live on my own in my house, but I definitely rely a lot more on reminders now, and I just put off things that used to be a normal part of my routine.
Have you noticed any significant change in the way your clothes fit you over the past year?

Well, yes, they are fitting a bit differently. Actually, that's what made me come in to see someone. My eating has gotten all turned around lately. Some days I just completely forget to eat lunch. But then other days, I'll find myself just standing at the kitchen counter, eating crackers and sweets... even though nothing really tastes right to me anymore. It's just very irregular now.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past year?

I haven't stepped on a scale to know the exact number of pounds, to be honest. But like I was just saying a moment ago, my eating has just gotten completely turned around. Because I forget lunch entirely some days, and then other days I'm just standing at the counter eating sweets and crackers—even though nothing tastes right to me. So I'm just not eating proper, regular meals anymore, and I'm sure that's why my weight has dropped.
Would you say your weight loss over the past year has been noticeable to others?

Well, I suppose so, since my clothes are fitting differently. But really, like I said, the main thing that brought me in is just how mixed up my eating has gotten. Some days I just don't eat lunch at all, I completely forget. And then other times I'm just standing there at the counter, eating sweets and crackers, even though food doesn't even taste right to me anymore. It's just all turned around.
Do you think you would start eating normally again if your low mood improved?

I'm really not sure about that. I haven't thought about it that way. I just know that right now, my appetite is completely off and nothing seems to appeal to me. I suppose it's possible things might get better if I wasn't feeling so down, but I just don't know for certain.
Do you think your eating patterns would go back to normal if your mood improved?

Well, I think you just asked me that, doctor. And honestly, like I was just saying, I really don't know for sure. I suppose it makes sense that if I wasn't feeling so down all the time, my appetite might come back, but... I just can't say for certain. I haven't really thought about it like that.
Are you upset or worried about the weight loss you've experienced over the past year?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm not happy about it, but I wouldn't say I'm worried or upset. It's just... it's just something that's happening, I guess. I'm more bothered by the fact that I just don't care about food anymore. The weight loss is just a result of that, you know?
Do you think your eating would return to normal if your mood improved?

Doctor, I believe you've asked me that three times now. Like I told you just a moment ago, I really don't know. I suppose it might, but I just can't say for sure. I don't really have a different answer to give you.
Are you concerned about the weight loss itself, regardless of how it's affecting your daily life?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit, doctor. Like I just said, I'm not really upset or worried about it. It's just a thing that's happening because I don't have an appetite. I wouldn't say I'm concerned about the weight loss itself, no.
Do you think your eating problems would improve if your depression got better?
Doctor, I... I really don't mean to be difficult, but you just asked me that exact same question. I don't know if my eating would get better if my mood improved. I just don't know.
